style.vernacular: Dry-savanna Pacific capital: low 1-2 storey concrete-block and rendered buildings with long-span corrugated-iron roofs, louvre windows and deep verandas; stilted timber and iron houses in the Motu villages (Hanuabada, Porebada); compounds behind tall metal-sheeted fences and razor wire; a handful of glass towers and modern government blocks at Waigani and the harbour; parched ochre-brown hills with eucalyptus and acacia, palms on the coast.
style.ornament: Sepik haus tambaran-style steep gabled roofs and carved ceremonial motifs on national buildings (Parliament House, museum); painted murals and tribal patterns on boundary walls; Motu lakatoi-sail and stilt-house references at Hanuabada; security grilles and sheeted fences everywhere.

sources.what: Parliament House (1984) blends traditional design with modern building technology; Boroko, Waigani, Hanuabada; homes with big fences covered in metal sheeting and steel security doors; tropical savanna climate
purpose-built national museum 1975-77 at Waigani; refurbished 2017 by Architectus
Populous-designed 2015 stadium with permanent roofed grandstand
